pr_body:
This patch adds a prometheus endpoint to the roachtest process and a
prometheus metric factory which roachtest writers can use to create their own
metrics.

Fixes https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/94694

Release note: none
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/94711)
first commit is used merely to show an example of how this endpoint could be used, which will merge in the next day or two.

> This patch adds a prometheus endpoint to the roachtest process and a prometheus metric factory which roachtest writers can use to create their own metrics.

Apropos the latter, I am a bit fuzzy on whether we need (and even should expose) a prom metric factory. We seem to have a nice, internal metrics API (pkg/util/metric/metric.go) which is used pervasively throughout the codebase. After a recent refactoring [1], HDRHistogram was replaced by prometheus.Histogram which reduced the memory footprint; it relies on custom buckets (e.g., `IOLatencyBuckets`) to maintain high precision. The internal API implements `ToPrometheusMetric`; that's how all the internal metrics are exposed via the prom endpoint. The benefit of using this API is it might be more idiomatic; e.g., an idiomatic way of creating a windowed histogram to measure duration in [10 micros, 10 seconds],

```
metric.NewHistogram("wait_duration" base.DefaultHistogramWindowInterval(), metric.IOLatencyBuckets)
```

Another potential benefit is reduced memory (and storage) footprint for histograms.
Strangely enough, workloads (still) use `HDRHistogram` but they use the internal metrics API for counters and gauges; e.g., [2]. 

Note, I've only taken a cursory look at the internal metrics API, so I am not aware of its deficiencies. I mainly wanted to start a discussion on the merits of exposing the prom API to the test writer.

[1] https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/81181
[2] https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/38d207af32dbc568982f95ac6eb8c66b0bfc03cf/pkg/workload/tpcc/worker.go#L108

Good questions! I decided not to use cockroach's internal metric's package as I think it's exclusively used by a cockroach process and will persist metrics to cockroach's time series database (TSDB). At least that's how I read the package's doc's page [1]. Given that the roachtest process doesn't need to or have direct access to the cockroach TSDB, the metrics package didn't seem like an appropriate fit here.

Also, I might be wrong, but I don't think the workload metric code relies on the crdb's metrics package at all, and instead, creates a prometheus registry in the same manner as I propose in this patch. Indeed, I used the workload code as a guide. E.g.
1. Here, we create a native prom registry [2]
2. Here in the tpcc workload setup, we create a prom factory and add new metrics in the same manner as my example in this PR. [3]

I do wonder if we ought to expose the roachtest writer directly to the prom factory though, given my comment [here](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/94711#discussion_r1063027562).

[1] https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/2675c7c0481bb33eb9f43f1c2b52c152fca3ae2d/pkg/util/metric/doc.go#L12

[2] https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/d711ba2278450b1b17943c7a3e11f0e08dfa241b/pkg/workload/histogram/histogram.go#L150
[3] https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/79a4d4ad2295d6cf69083d93022d9cf49557c6fa/pkg/workload/tpcc/worker.go#L97

> Good questions! I decided not to use cockroach's internal metric's package as I think it's exclusively used by a cockroach process and will persist metrics to cockroach's time series database (TSDB). At least that's how I read the package's doc's page [1]. Given that the roachtest process doesn't need to or have direct access to the cockroach TSDB, the metrics package didn't seem like an appropriate fit here.

That makes sense. However, the internal metrics API does appear to be fairly generic. Note, the metrics created via the API are not automatically exported (or persisted via TSDB). The setup happens in `PreStart` (server.go) where `recorder` is initialized with a shared `metric.Registry`. This registry is polled to record samples into TSDB (see `GetTimeSeriesData`) or scraped to export prometheus metrics (see `handleVars`). Thus, we could in theory use them strictly for prometheus.

> Also, I might be wrong, but I don't think the workload metric code relies on the crdb's metrics package at all, and instead, creates a prometheus registry in the same manner as I propose in this patch.

You're right. The workloads are indeed using prom's API. (I was misled by `NewCounter` which is in both APIs). I can't really comment on whether that was intentional... maybe the original author (@tbg) of the internal metrics API could chime in?

> I can't really comment on whether that was intentional... maybe the original author (@tbg) of the internal metrics API could chime in?

For me this is intentional. We shouldn't entangle the metrics code in CRDB with the very vanilla needs of roachtest.
@srosenberg just added an extra commit, which speeds up testrunner unit tests to avoid test time outs. If this looks good, I'll squash and merge.

Note the labels; `test_name` was added explicitly, the rest are generated from the metadata. Test Dashboard: https://grafana.testeng.crdb.io/d/I2_Fu704k/new-dashboard?orgId=1&from=now-5m&to=now&viewPanel=2

issue_context.title: roachtest: expose prometheus endpoint in roachtest process
issue_context.body:
Currently, a prometheus server can scrape metrics from the cockroach and workload processes, allowing the user to set up grafana dashboards to monitor their cluster(s). A roachtest writer may also want to construct and expose certain metrics for a prometheus server. Indeed, a prometheus endpoint on the roachtest process is one necessary step to deprecate roachperf in favor of grafana dashboard(s) that monitor roachtest performance over several runs.

To ensure the prom server scrapes all roachtest metrics, the roachtest process will need to sleep for one scrape_interval before shutting down. 

Jira issue: CRDB-23091

Epic CRDB-20915

review_comments: for each new metric the roachtest writer creates, I think we'd also want to apply the following labels: `cluster_id`, `host`, `cloud`, `release_branch` etc. I _think_ these can be applied via the prom server config, correct? If not, I'll probably need to construct an API around the `PromFactory()` so the roachtest write doesn't have to worry about that stuff.

`host` is part of the prom config [1]; we could easily add `cloud`; `cluster_id`, `release_branch` and other test-specific labels could be added by the roachtest (test_runner) via (cloud) metadata. E.g., prometheus config. currently exports `test_name` metadata label,

```
- source_labels: [__meta_gce_metadata_test_name]
    separator: ;
    regex: (.*)
    target_label: test_name
    replacement: ${1}
    action: replace
```

[1] https://grafana.testeng.crdb.io/prometheus/targets
Not sure what this is intended to test. This unit test is basically exercising the helper `PromSub`.
Exactly. Added better documentation to reflect this.
